newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian pipeline to move Russian crude - minister.
newsitem.headline: Croatian pipeline to move Russian crude - minister.

text.p: Croatia said on Tuesday talks were under way with the Russian oil industry on investing $120 million in the Adriatic pipeline to transport up to 14 million tonnes of Russian crude a year to the Mediterranean.
"The idea is three or four years old, but the talks started again last week," Minister of Economy Davor Stern told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Stern, who has had contacts with the Russian oil ministry and the Transneft oil pipeline company, said a deal could be reached by the end of January.

Russians are interested in finding an alternative route for transport of crude oil from central Asia to western Europe, and are prepared to invest some $120 million in upgrading a part of the Croatian pipeline that links the Adriatic port of Omisalj with the Druzhba (Friendship) pipeline on the Hungarian border.
"Some other (non-Russian) firms that exploit oil from Russia are interested in investing, or buying a share, in the Adriatic pipeline as well," Stern said.
He said that upgrading the Croatian pipeline would be a faster and cheaper solution than building a new one from the Bulgarian port of Bourgas to Alexandroupolis in Greece.
Russians are considering the latter idea as an alternative project to circumvent the overcrowded Bosphorous.
JANAF, the company running the Adriatic pipeline, is 100 percent state-owned but the government is planning to privatise it in the next three months, Stern said.

The proposed investment would enable a shipment of 10 to 14 million tonnes of oil per year. Omisalj terminal has enough unused storage facilities and is accessible to the big tankers to make the flow possible, Stern said. -- Davor Huic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
